summary.text: Robert Manger is a Republican who represents Oklahoma House District 101, which includes parts of Choctaw, part of Midwest City, Nicoma Park and parts of Oklahoma City. He was first elected in 2018, and in the 60th Legislature he chairs the Judiciary and Public Safety Oversight Committee.

paragraphs.text: Manger was born in Oklahoma City and graduated from Del City High School, and he earned a Bachelor of Arts in criminal justice from the University of Central Oklahoma and an Associate of Arts in sociology from Rose State College.

His public service career began in law enforcement in 1978 with the Oklahoma County Sheriff’s office, and in 1987 he joined the United States Marshals Service, where he served until his retirement in 2011.
His House biography says he has also worked as a realtor in the Oklahoma City metro area for over 12 years.
Manger is a member of the Appropriations and Budget Committee, the Veterans and Military Affairs Committee and the Criminal Judiciary Committee.

His page says he authored a bill signed into law in 2024 that made combining fentanyl with other controlled substances a felony, and a law in 2023 making a first offense of domestic abuse against a pregnant woman a felony.
Manger and his wife have been married for over 40 years and have lived in District 101 for over 30 years.
